review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the row indices from col through n-1 as a finite search domain. Mark an index k exactly when abs(rows[k][col]) is at least every active-column magnitude and is strictly greater than every magnitude at an earlier active index, thereby reproducing Python max's first-index tie rule. Use Grover-style search only to propose this unique pivot index.

Encode col, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 values rows[i][col]. A reversible predicate must implement Python-compatible absolute value, ordering, equality, signed-zero behavior, and first-index tie handling over all active rows. Coherent loading, representation of nonfinite intermediate state, ancilla cleanup, and gate costs remain unresolved.
Although inputs are validated as finite binary64 values, the predicate consumes dynamically updated elimination state and may need to represent nonfinite intermediates consistently.

binding.rationale: The primary predicate explicitly requires at least every active magnitude and strictly greater than every earlier active magnitude. Translate both universal comparisons literally, including self in every active index. No finite-value admission guard is supplied; nonfinite representation is explicitly unresolved, not excluded. Do not substitute an ordered scan or use the classical verifier to repair this marking predicate.

interpretations.meaning: At least every active value and strictly greater than all earlier values.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[j] for j in indices) and all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i)
